title: POC scoping: Private networking & data residency - MediCore Health
summary: AE and SE scoped a 6-week POC focused on private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency (US-only), and performance benchmarks. Agreed success criteria: latency targets, throughput, and no cross-border egress. Next steps: share network diagram & security pack, schedule benchmark window, kickoff week-of Oct 13.
next_steps: Redwood: send private networking diagram + security pack (SOC2, HIPAA note) by 2025-10-06
Customer: provide VPC CIDR ranges and peering contact by 2025-10-07
Schedule benchmark window (two 2-hour windows) week of 2025-10-20
action_items: Maya Chen (AE): Email pricing and POC SOW draft by 2025-10-06
Liam Patel (SE): Prepare benchmark plan + load script and estimate infra by 2025-10-10
Priya Desai (Customer): Share VPC CIDRs and peering engineer contact by 2025-10-07
Ravi Kumar (Customer Security): Confirm KMS/HSM integration constraints and DLP requirements by 2025-10-09
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-03 15:00 UTC (52 minutes)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Alvarez (CTO, MediCore), Priya Desai (Head of Infra), Ravi Kumar (Security)

00:00 Maya Chen: thanks everyone for joining, uh we know everyone's busy so we'll try to be tight on time. quick intro, i'm maya, i'm the account exec on this. liam is our se, he'll own the technical bit.
00:18 Tom Alvarez: yeah thanks, maya. quick context, we're evaluating a POC with you all for inference for patient-facing summarization and triage workflows. main constraints are data must remain in us-only, and we need private connectivity — no traffic across the public internet.
00:36 Liam Patel: great, thanks tom. we'll focus today on VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress controls, regions, and then map that to success criteria and a benchmark plan. sound good?
00:47 Priya Desai: yep, that's right. we also have some throughput targets — at peak the app needs ~120 requests per minute with median payload around 400 tokens, and some larger batched jobs during off hours. latency is important for the triage flows.
01:05 Ravi Kumar: and from security, we need audit logs, KMS integration, and verification that no logs or data leave the chosen region. also HIPAA considerations, so proof of SOC2 is helpful.
01:20 Maya Chen: mm-hmm. quick note on our deployment options: for this POC we'd propose Redwood Private deployed into your VPC via one of two network patterns — VPC peering (classic) or AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). we can also do transit gateway connections for multi-VPC setups; we'll outline tradeoffs.
01:38 Tom Alvarez: could you run through the tradeoffs briefly please? peering vs private link — specifically around cross-account and cross-region constraints.
01:46 Liam Patel: sure. VPC peering is straightforward for same-region peering, low overhead, and full network reachability. downside: it's point-to-point and doesn't scale well if you have many VPCs. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is regional only as well, but gives a managed endpoint in your VPC and keeps published IPs owned by AWS, so it's easier for egress control and we don't require route table changes. transit gateway helps scale for many VPCs and cross-account routing but adds cost. also note PrivateLink hides our service behind AWS network endpoints which customers often prefer for private connectivity and private DNS.
02:25 Priya Desai: ok and what about cross-region? our primary region must be us-east-1, we may want eu-west-1 later for EU patients but for now US residency is top requirement. can your private deployment be pinned to a region to guarantee no egress?
02:40 Liam Patel: yes. Redwood Private can be deployed in a specified region and we can ensure that inference, KV cache, and logs remain in that region. our control-plane connectivity is out-of-band — for Private deployments we can also run a customer-managed control plane if needed to further limit egress. we'll capture the deployment model in the security pack.
02:58 Ravi Kumar: what's the canonical way you prove 'no egress' to auditors? we need audit trails and evidence.
03:08 Maya Chen: good question. typically we provide network diagrams, VPC flow logs, audit logs from our runtime, and SOC2 attestation. for HIPAA we have BAAs available — we'll include that in the pack. also KMS integration: we support customer-managed KMS keys for at-rest encryption and can integrate with HSMs in some cases.
03:28 Tom Alvarez: thanks. can you outline the success criteria you usually see for these POCs? specific numbers help.
03:36 Liam Patel: sure — based on similar healthcare pilots, customers often set: p50 latency <150ms for 256-token responses, p95 <350ms, p99 <600ms for synchronous chat; throughput target 8-10 qps sustained per instance, and end-to-end median under 200ms for the triage short prompts. for embeddings/async jobs we'd measure throughput and batch efficiency; quality metric is accuracy of summaries against a small labeled set (we usually run an eval with ~200 samples).
04:10 Priya Desai: those latency numbers — are they from Redwood hosted or private? we need them from the private deployment topology since network hop matters.
04:19 Liam Patel: good point. the numbers I quoted are typical for dedicated/private deployments on similar GPU shapes in us-east-1. during the POC we'll run the benchmark from your network (we can run the client in your VPC) to measure true end-to-end.
04:34 Tom Alvarez: what's the recommended hardware? we have existing infra budget for a small GPU fleet.
04:40 Liam Patel: for these workloads we'd recommend an A100-class or H100 if you're doing large context models; if you care more about cost and the model supports quantization we often recommend a mixed fleet (some cheaper GPU shapes for inference). for the POC we can scope a minimal fleet of 2 GPUs to validate latency and failover.
04:58 Maya Chen: timeline question — you're looking at a decision after the POC? what's your target?
05:03 Tom Alvarez: ideally a go/no-go in 6 weeks. procurement cycle is separate but we'd like to have performance validation before committing.
05:10 Maya Chen: good, that lines up with our standard 4–6 week POC. we'll propose a 6-week plan: week 0 network setup and security kickoff, week 1–2 deploy and smoke tests, week 3 benchmark runs, week 4 tuning & reruns, week 5 wrap-up + evaluation, week 6 decision.
05:34 Priya Desai: for the network setup, who is the peering owner on your side? and do you need a specific CIDR allocation?
05:42 Maya Chen: we'll own the coordination from Redwood side; Liam will provide a detailed diagram and the endpoint IP ranges you need to allow. we usually request non-overlapping CIDRs; for PrivateLink you just need to allow interface endpoint ENIs — we'll include specifics.
05:58 Liam Patel: i'll put together a network diagram showing both peering and PrivateLink options, plus the necessary security group and route table changes.
06:06 Ravi Kumar: about encryption in transit — do you use mTLS between your nodes and our clients?
06:11 Liam Patel: yes. for private deployments we support mutual TLS and we can require client certs. additionally, all control-plane communications can be restricted to specific IPs and VPC endpoints.
06:23 Tom Alvarez: i want to call out egress constraints: legal requires that data not transit through third countries. if your control plane is global, how do you guarantee that?
06:34 Maya Chen: we have two patterns: managed control plane where some metadata may go to our hosted control plane (we can limit metadata scope), or a customer-managed control plane deployed in your account/VPC which ensures control traffic stays inside your region. for strict legal requirements we recommend customer-managed control plane.
06:53 Priya Desai: ok, and logging retention — we don't want full transcript retention longer than 30 days, is that configurable?
07:00 Liam Patel: yes, retention policies are configurable. for POC we'll set a 30-day retention and can redact PII from logs as part of the pipeline; we'll document that.
07:10 Tom Alvarez: about benchmarking — what does the benchmark plan look like?
07:14 Liam Patel: we'll run two types of benchmarks: synthetic load to measure throughput/latency distribution (qps sweeps, batch size sweeps), and a functional quality run against your labeled samples. proposed load: 10-minute sustained windows at 8 qps, 30-minute ramp test, and spike tests to exercise autoscaling. metrics we collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and model output diffs vs baseline.
07:40 Priya Desai: where will the load generator run from? we want to ensure the path matches real traffic — ideally inside our VPC.
07:47 Liam Patel: yes, we recommend running the load generator inside your VPC (we can provide a small EC2 spec). we'll also run a second generator from an external region to measure cross-region characteristics.
07:58 Ravi Kumar: can you sign a BAA?
08:02 Maya Chen: yes, we can. we'll include our legal/BAA template in the security pack.
08:07 Tom Alvarez: backups and DR — any notes?
08:12 Liam Patel: for POC we recommend snapshotting models and configs. long-term we offer replication across AZs; cross-region replication can be added but that may affect residency constraints so we'll treat as optional for later stages.
08:28 Priya Desai: i'd like to hear about observability — can we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns?
08:35 Maya Chen: yes. Redwood Console exposes per-request latency, per-token breakdown, and cost estimates. for private deployments we can push metrics to your CloudWatch/Prometheus as well.
08:48 Tom Alvarez: ok, let's talk SLOs — what SLOs do you typically commit to for a dedicated/private deployment POC?
08:55 Maya Chen: for pilot POCs we don't usually push an SLA until production, but we can commit to availability targets for the duration and create runbooks. if you move to a dedicated contract we have SLA terms with uptime and latency targets.
09:06 Priya Desai: procurement will want network diagrams and a clear list of ports and IPs. please include that.
09:12 Liam Patel: noted. i'll attach a one-page network checklist with ports (443, ephemeral for mTLS), CIDR guidance, and PrivateLink ENI behavior.
09:22 Tom Alvarez: are there any additional costs for PrivateLink vs peering?
09:27 Maya Chen: PrivateLink does have AWS interface endpoint costs and additional per-GB data processing charges at AWS level; we can include an estimated cost delta in the pricing spreadsheet.
09:36 Ravi Kumar: how do you handle key management — can we supply our KMS key?
09:41 Liam Patel: yes, customer-managed KMS keys are supported for data at rest; for additional HSM requirements we can engage the product team — there's some extra integration work.
09:52 Priya Desai: one more — do you have any examples of customers who pinned to a single-region private deployment and had auditors sign off?
09:58 Maya Chen: yes, we've done several healthcare pilots where customers used a customer-managed control plane in their VPC and auditors validated the logs and flow logs. i'll include anonymized references in the security pack.
10:12 Tom Alvarez: great. can you summarize the exact success criteria we'll use for the POC so we can align on pass/fail?
10:20 Liam Patel: sure — proposed success criteria: (1) Functional: 85%+ accuracy on labeled summary set; (2) Performance: p50 latency <150ms, p95 <350ms, p99 <600ms for our triage prompts under the 8 qps sustained load; (3) Network/security: all traffic stays in us-east-1, no egress outside US, customer-managed KMS in place; (4) Ops: logs available in your CloudWatch, and audit evidence for retention + redaction policies.
11:03 Maya Chen: and decision rule? if two of four categories fail we consider it a no-go, otherwise we'll discuss mitigations.
11:12 Tom Alvarez: sounds fair. procurement will also need a statement of work and estimated costs.
11:18 Maya Chen: we'll send a draft SOW and pricing.
11:22 Priya Desai: for the benchmark windows, we prefer nights 02:00–04:00 ET to minimize production impact.
11:29 Liam Patel: that works; we'll propose two 2-hour windows during week of Oct 20 (night windows).
11:36 Ravi Kumar: are you able to provide an SLA for data deletion after 30 days?
11:40 Maya Chen: yes for the POC we will set retention to 30 days and provide deletion proofs (logs). we'll document the deletion workflow.
11:48 Tom Alvarez: any caveats around model updates during POC? we want a stable model artifact for the duration.
11:54 Liam Patel: we'll pin the model version for the POC and record the model hash. any updates require a formal change request.
12:03 Priya Desai: okay awesome. next steps recap?
12:07 Maya Chen: recap — we'll send network diagram + security pack + pricing + SOW by Monday 2025-10-06. liam will follow up with benchmark plan and load scripts by 2025-10-10. you (pri ya) will share VPC CIDRs and peering contact by 2025-10-07. schedule benchmark for week of Oct 20.
12:29 Tom Alvarez: noted. anything else?
12:33 Ravi Kumar: just ensure the security pack includes BAAs and SOC2 scope.
12:37 Maya Chen: will do. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and set up the kickoff call for week of Oct 13.
12:47 Tom Alvarez: great, thanks.
12:49 Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., Redwood Private sometimes transcribed informally as 'Redwood Privet'), filler words retained.
